text:
Alex K: Heads-up — regression on prefill path with INT8 kernels for long contexts (>16k). Dumping profiles, TL;DR prefill latency up ~1.8x while decode TPS still higher than FP16.
perf-bot: perf alert: prefill_p99 increased from 210ms -> 380ms for redwood-13b-quant on cluster-gpu-3 (tag: int8).
Maria P: Can you paste the profiler output and TTFT/TPS numbers?
Alex K: Sure — quick snippets from nvprof / perf traces:
```
# timeline (ms)
prefill: 512 tokens 
  FP16 baseline: p50 210ms, p99 260ms, TTFT 18ms, TPS ~5.1k
  INT8 (current): p50 360ms, p99 380ms, TTFT 45ms, TPS ~6.8k
decode (streaming 1 token):
  FP16: 4.9k TPS, TTFT 12ms
  INT8: 6.9k TPS, TTFT 14ms
# kernel hotspots (sample)
  layer3_linear: int8_gemm_kernel_fallback 42% (mem-bound stalls)
  kv_write: 18% (large contiguous writes)
  attention_qk: int8_attn_fast 10%
  GPU occupancy: ~73%
```
Sam T: Interesting — decode faster on int8 (good) but prefill much worse. Kernel selector looks like it's choosing a slower fallback for some MLP layers when activation ranges exceed calibrated thresholds.
Jordan L: My guess is memory bandwidth + KV write pattern during prefill is causing stalls. Prefill writes full KV for every token (big stride), decode is incremental and can reuse caches => TPS vs TTFT tradeoff.
Rahul S: Also check batching heuristics — batcher might be waiting to reach min_batch_size for prefill requests, raising TTFT. Prefill tends to come in big single requests but sometimes we group small ones which hurts latency.
Maria P: Which calibration was used when quantizing? Per-channel static with 128 calibration steps? Overestimation can push some blocks out of efficient kernel path.
Alex K: Yes, we used static histogram calibration (128 steps) and a conservative clipping threshold. The selector then picks the INT8 fallback that uses an extra dequant->compute->requant step for certain matmuls.
Sam T: That explains the mem copies. If the kernel does dequant->FP32 GEMM->requant for certain shapes, memory bandwidth and extra passes blow up for prefill. For decode the matmuls are smaller so kernel still wins.
Jordan L: From profiling the big offenders are MLP FC2 for layers 2..6 — shape is (batch * seq, hidden) so prefill multiplies sequence length times, making it heavy.
Maria P: Options: 1) rerun calibration with per-channel AJUSTED percentile (e.g., 99.5 -> 99.9) to lower fallback count, 2) adjust kernel selector cost model to penalize dequant passes more for large sequence sizes, 3) change batching window for prefill to avoid TTFT spikes.
Alex K: Quick experiments I ran:
```
# experiment A - aggressive calibration (reduce clipping)
int8_fallback_rate: 28% -> 12%
prefill p50: 360ms -> 290ms (better but still above FP16)
# experiment B - selector tweak (prefer no-requant kernel for seq>4k)
fallback rate: 28% -> 5%
prefill p50: 360ms -> 230ms (close to FP16)
# experiment C - batcher window 8ms -> 4ms (reduce TTFT)
TTFT: 45ms -> 28ms but overall p50 only -10ms due to kernel cost
```
Rahul S: Good. Experiment B looks promising but might regress accuracy if the no-requant kernel isn't well-calibrated. Need to run evals on regression set.
Sam T: Agree. Also monitor GPU memory traffic counters — if we can keep big matmul on int8 native path (no dequant), prefill wins.
Maria P: Action items: Alex to run accuracy eval for experiment B and full rollout simulation; Sam to add a cost-weight for dequant passes into the kernel selector; Rahul to prototype a prefill-specific batching config that reduces TTFT without hurting throughput.
Alex K: I'll post the eval results by EOD + attach perf flamegraphs.
Jordan L: One more thought — KV cache layout: consider block-compressed KV layout for INT8 to reduce bandwidth during prefill writes. Longer-term but could help big contexts.
Maria P: Nice. @perf-bot will you add a perf regression ticket and attach these logs? :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Created PERF-1427: prefill-int8-p99-regression. Logs attached.
Sam T: Thanks — let's keep changes staged behind rollout flags.
Alex K: ACK, thanks all.
